class.name: RadioDecoder
class.brief_description: Generic audio decoder class providing a common interface for audio stream decoders with buffering support.
class.description:
[RadioDecoder] is the base class for audio stream decoders. It handles the whole path from encoded data to audio frames: - incoming encoded data is stored in a fixed 128 KiB buffer (about 8 seconds at 128 kbps). If the buffer is full, the oldest bytes are dropped and [signal buffer_overrun] is emitted. This keeps playback close to live after a stall. - [method process_audio] decodes the data one codec frame at a time and pushes the result into an [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback]. - it tracks the buffering state and emits signals when buffering starts and finishes. Decoding starts only after about one second of encoded data is buffered (see [method set_bitrate_hint]). When the codec runs out of data, the same amount is buffered again before decoding continues. The format of the first decoded frame is reported through [signal stream_info_ready]. Format changes during the stream are described there. [RadioStream] creates a decoder for the server's content type by itself, and [RadioPlayer] does all the remaining steps, so most users do not use this class directly.
[b]Note:[/b] Derived classes only implement the codec (decode one frame, reset). Everything else is shared. Decoders are C++ classes; the codec methods are not available to scripts.

signal.name: buffering_started
signal.description: Emitted when the buffered audio data has been depleted and the decoder enters the buffering state. Emitted synchronously from [method process_audio].

signal.name: buffering_finished
signal.description: Emitted when the buffered audio data reaches the configured target threshold and buffering completes. Emitted synchronously from [method process_audio].

signal.name: stream_info_ready
signal.description: Emitted from inside [method process_audio] (directly, on the main thread) after the decoder has decoded the first frame of the stream and knows its sample rate and channel count. No playback is needed yet at this point, so a handler can set the generator's [code]mix_rate[/code] from [method get_stream_sample_rate], start the player, and then call [method set_playback] with the new playback. The first frame is kept and pushed as soon as a playback is set. Nothing else is decoded until then. [b]Note:[/b] The signal can be emitted more than once per stream. Some stations change the sample rate between tracks (for example when switching to a fallback source or an ad). The generator's [code]mix_rate[/code] cannot change while playing, so the decoder emits this signal again, and the handler should do the same steps with a new playback. A change between mono and stereo is handled inside the decoder and does not emit the signal.

signal.name: buffer_overrun
signal.description: Emitted when incoming encoded data arrives faster than it is consumed and the internal jitter buffer (128 KiB) overflows. The oldest [param dropped_bytes] bytes are discarded so playback stays near the live edge. Stations that open with a large burst of data cause this in normal use. Repeated overruns during playback mean [method process_audio] is not being called regularly. The signal is emitted deferred because the overflow is detected on the download thread.

signal.name: stream_error
signal.description: Emitted from inside [method process_audio] (synchronously, on the main thread) when the decoder has failed to detect the stream format twice in a row. Each attempt consumes the buffered data, so this usually means the stream is not in the format the decoder was created for (for example AAC served with an [code]audio/mpeg[/code] content type). The decoder keeps trying; the handler should typically cancel the request. Emitted once per stream; [method reset] re-arms it.

method.name: set_playback
method.description: Sets the [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback] instance used by the decoder for buffer management. This playback object is used to determine the current buffering state and available audio frames. The maximum buffer capacity is observed directly from the playback's ring buffer rather than computed, so no generator or capacity value needs to be supplied. Call this again with a freshly instantiated playback whenever the generator's [code]mix_rate[/code] or [code]buffer_length[/code] changes.

method.name: set_buffer_thresholds
method.description: Configures the buffering threshold used by the decoder. [code]target_frames[/code] is the number of buffered frames needed before buffering is considered complete. A value larger than the playback can hold is limited to the playback's capacity (with a warning printed once), because it could never be reached.

method.name: process_audio
method.description: Processes decoder-specific audio handling and moves raw audio frame data into the [AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback]'s ring buffer. Call it regularly (e.g. from a [Timer] or [method Node._process]); the decoder sizes its work to the space available in the playback. [b]Note:[/b] Must be called from the main thread. All signals raised from it ([signal buffering_started], [signal buffering_finished] and [signal stream_info_ready]) are emitted directly, not deferred, so their handlers run before this method returns.

method.name: reset
method.description: Discards all buffered encoded data, the codec state and the probe-failure count, so the decoder probes the stream again from scratch. Use it to reuse one decoder instance across reconnects instead of creating a new one. Must be called from the main thread.

method.name: set_bitrate_hint
method.description: Sets how much encoded data (in bytes) must be buffered before decoding starts, and before it continues after the codec has run out of data. The amount is about one second of audio at [param kbps]: [code]max((kbps * 1000) / 8, 16384)[/code]. Streams below 128 kbps all use the minimum of 16384 bytes, which for them is more than one second. If this method is not called, the minimum is used for the first frame, and after that the bitrate reported by the codec is used (MP3 reports it). Values of [code]0[/code] or less are ignored. [RadioStream] calls this with the value of the server's [code]icy-br[/code] header on the decoders it creates.

method.name: get_stream_sample_rate
method.description: Returns the sample rate of the stream, as last reported by [signal stream_info_ready], or [code]0[/code] before the signal was emitted for the first time.

method.name: get_stream_channels
method.description: Returns the channel count of the last decoded frame, or [code]0[/code] until [signal stream_info_ready] has been emitted. It can change during the stream without a signal.

method.name: get_buffering_progress
method.description: Returns the current buffering progress as a value between [code]0.0[/code] and [code]1.0[/code].

method.name: is_buffering
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the decoder is currently buffering audio data, otherwise returns [code]false[/code].

method.name: get_current_target_frames
method.description: Returns the current target number of buffered frames required before playback can resume after buffering.

method.name: get_current_max_capacity_frames
method.description: Returns the observed maximum capacity of the playback ring buffer, expressed in audio frames. Intended for debugging.

method.name: create_for_mime_type
method.description: Creates and returns a new decoder for [code]mime_type[/code] (for example [code]"audio/mpeg"[/code]), or [code]null[/code] if no decoder is registered for that MIME type. Decoders register themselves when the extension is loaded. [RadioStream] uses this method to create a decoder for each connection. Scripts only need it to use a decoder without the stream.
